title: Jon Martin — Field Report & Second Opinion
description: Capacity is more of what you already do. Range is more of what you can absorb. Founder-led $3–5M professional services firms keep breaking because the last hire, tool, SOP, and manager added capacity without adding range.
heroTitle: You are the only person in your company with enough range to handle what comes at it.
subhead: Capacity is more of what you already do. Range is more of what you can absorb. Every fix you've tried — the hire, the software, the SOP, the management layer — added capacity. That's why it kept breaking anyway.
tagline: I don't build it. I tell you why the last three things you built didn't work.
whoParagraphs: Founders of professional services businesses doing $3–5M in revenue — agencies, consultancies, MSPs, engineering and design firms. Somewhere between twenty and fifty people. Still founder-led, still founder-dependent: you're still the best seller, often still the best deliverer, and still in the loop on everything that matters.

This is not a build engagement, an implementation partner, or a coaching package. If the last three things you built didn't hold, the next hire or tool will fail in the same place unless the constraint is named first.
offerStatement: I don't build it. I tell you why the last three things you built didn't work.
fourFixesHeading: Why did the last four fixes fail?
fourFixes: You hired someone senior and they can't operate without you.
You bought software and nobody trusts what it reports.
You wrote SOPs and nobody follows them.
You added a layer of management and it turned into a game of telephone.
convergenceLine: Each of those looks like a separate problem. It isn't. They are four readings of the same missing thing: range.
distinctionHeading: Capacity is more of what you already do. Range is more of what you can absorb.
capacityCaption: Seven of the same response. Handles more volume of what you've already seen.
rangeCaption: Seven different responses. Handles the kinds of thing you haven't seen yet.
